questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I wanted to experience the british university culture and live in Edinburgh. Also I wanted to hike and explore the nature in Scotland.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Fairly easy, the university of Edinburgh was incredibly helpful and go quite far to help you in your individual situation.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: The student support system at the University of Edinburgh is very well developed, so it was easy to get help if needed.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: I found my housing through the university. Because of a larger than normal intake of first year students possibilities were limited, so it was not until very last minute I got an offer of housing with the university.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: It is good to know that offers of housing for exchange students is not guaranteed, but there is a very good chance of getting something (however price and location can vary a lot). Be aware that the offer for housing can come very last minute, I was already a week into my stay in Edinburgh when I got the offer and could move in the same day. The accommodation office is very helpful, so always reach out to them (also during the stay) if any advice or help is needed on the housing situation.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: It was easy to register for regular courses when you apply for the University in the first place. Spots in honors courses are offered later, but for me it was easy to get into those that I wanted.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: The university is generally really helpful and very easy to get in contact with.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got the courses I wanted.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: The University of Edinburgh is much more understanding of missing deadlines or filling something out wrong in the application process than KU, so don't be afraid to make mistakes in the process - they are really there to help you.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The teaching is mostly good and engaging, but there is very little in class teaching.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: It was fine. I took courses a bit away from "core" legal courses and had courses with students studying for different degrees, so they were very aware to explain things and include everyone.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: I originally though it would be a bit more engaging and debating at the University of Edinburgh, but it was generally mostly the professor speaking. There is much less group work for the classes.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: International criminal law, Slavery in eighteenth century Scotland and Introduction to Criminology.

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I really liked Criminology. The teaching is good and it is not too time consuming.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: Housing was more expensive than expected: you only get on offer of housing from the university and the price on their housing can vary a lot, also finding independent housing is difficult and expensive in Edinburgh at the moment.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Prices are generally lower in Edinburgh - also trains across the country are sensibly priced, so it is easy to travel into the Highlands.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: There are so many clubs and societies, you can do anything you would want. People are really welcoming and it is easy to get to know people in these settings.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Any clubs that interests you.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Go into the Highlands and spend time exploring Edinburgh.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Very easy, Edinburgh is really a university city and everyone is incredibly friendly.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Join the clubs and societies.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: None. Edinburgh is a very international city so expect to meet people from all over the world and not just Scotland in the social activities - maybe actually finding a Scottish person to talk to was the most difficult challenge.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: People are very welcoming and friendly.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Definitely go. It is easy to adjust in Edinburgh, people are friendly and teaching is good.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: No

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Meeting great people and exploring Scotland

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: There weren't really many challenges - I think finding housing in the beginning was the most difficult.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
